text:
[LLEX.9.5] An author must not declare an identifier that is a
reserved word, and the compiler must refuse such a declaration. The
reserved words are the rows of [LLEX.9.6], the percentile family and `_`,
below. The restriction binds at
every site an author names something — a slot, a binding, a schema, a
rule, a `const`, a service kwarg, and an `opaque type` — and admits no
position, scope or class in which a reserved word becomes nameable.

A word is reserved as one exact NFC string, so reservation is
case-sensitive on the terms [LNAM.2.1.1] already sets: `where` is
refused, and `Where` and `WHERE` are ordinary identifiers. An author
who meets a reserved word renames; DS supplies no quoted-identifier
form.

**The restriction binds an author's declarations, and nothing else.** A
schema the compiler itself declares may name a slot with a reserved word.
Reading such a slot is a read, not a declaration, so it is admissible in any
position a slot read is.

The percentile aggregations are the one reserved vocabulary that is a
family rather than a set of words. Every `p1` … `p99` is reserved, and
[LLEX.9.6] carries no row for any of them.

The identifier `_` alone is reserved and has no meaning. It is a `NAME`
([LLEX.10.4]), no construct gives it a meaning, and [LLEX.9.6] carries no row for
it. Nothing declares it, so a read of it is a read of an undeclared name.

alloy.name: llex_9_5__schema_kind_never_an_author_name
alloy.note: The kind Schema, reserved as type on LLEX.9.6, is spelled by no author identifier: the rule applied to that row. Fails if the kind's reservation is removed from names.als.
